correctness.rationale: The exact three-step affine solutions are computed in RESULT.md, with determinant S, first coordinate signs N0,N1,N2 and real 2x2 strict Jury inequalities. The LRR obstruction K is an explicit positive square unless c=d=1, excluded by c>|1+d|. A constructive v-then-u perturbation proves the golden-edge open set without evaluating at a non-saddle boundary. Exact rational witness and a 1056-assertion checker corroborate the equations. Limits: no global attractor or neutral/border orbits proven.

originality.rationale: The 2024 paper analyzes the identical two-saddle four-parameter map but its full available text develops renormalisation, crises and some low-period windows, not a complete period-three itinerary sign classification or the saddle-edge golden-ratio construction. The 2022 paper reports stable LLR dynamics outside the two-saddle domain and explicit general word stability and opposite-sign LRR tongues; neither claim covers the strict two-saddle iff and sign-square exclusion. The related public four-cycle obstruction is for a different length-four word. The work uses classical affine elimination and Schur tests, claiming originality only for their structural consequence and the explicit edge strip. Inaccessible full text of a 2016 survey leaves residual priority risk.
residual_risks: A sufficiently general treatment in Simpson (2016) or unindexed resonance-tongue work may already derive the specific symbolic and saddle-edge consequences. Full 2016 text was not accessible; no claim of having inspected it.
No assertion of priority outside inspected sources, and no assertion that existence of stable LLR cycles is new in the unrestricted normal form.

value.rationale: The 2024 two-saddle bifurcation study must distinguish chaotic basins from stable low-period windows. A necessary-and-sufficient prime-three parameter test, an exact forbidden reverse itinerary, and the golden-ratio threshold for an explicit saddle-edge window replace ambiguous numerical snapshots with a complete sharp period-three statement in a motivated family; the golden threshold is not claimed as a global bound.
